notes: Simple 4-node loop drawn as two stacked meshes. Net map: n1 = left vertical rail at x~155 joining the left terminal of I-DC 0 (3A) to the left terminal of Inductor 5 (20uH); n2 = short horizontal from the right terminal of I-DC 0 to the left terminal of Resistor 2 (750R); n3 = node at x~311 where the right terminal of Resistor 2 arrives, turns UP to y~198 and runs right into the left plate of Capacitor 4 (3uF), and also continues right into the '-' terminal of V-DC 1 (7V) -- verified at 7x, the vertical at x~311 is one unbroken stroke from the resistor/V-DC horizontal up to the capacitor horizontal, so cap-left, R-right and V-DC(-) are one net; 0 = the whole bottom/right return path: right terminal of Inductor 5 -> down -> bottom rail at y~305..315 -> GND 3 (T-stub dropping off the rail at x~277) -> continues right to x~404 -> up the right vertical, where the '+' terminal of V-DC 1 T-joins at y~258, and on up to y~211 and left into the right plate of Capacitor 4. Judgment calls: (a) the right vertical at x~404 is a single continuous stroke from the bottom rail to the capacitor's right lead (7x crop confirms no break and no hop), so Capacitor 4 right plate, V-DC 1 '+' and the GND rail are all net 0 -- the capacitor sits directly across the 7V source; (b) the large tilted quadrilateral running off all four edges of the frame is the scanned page border, not circuit wire; at 7x it passes ~50 px above the top-right circuit corner and below-left of the bottom rail and never touches a component lead; (c) 2-terminal index order is left-then-right as drawn for I-DC 0, Resistor 2, Capacitor 4 and Inductor 5, and '-'-then-'+' for V-DC 1 (order does not affect any metric); (d) I-DC 0 arrow points right, so conventional current flows into the resistor node; (e) no component is unconnected -- every lead lands on one of the four nets.
